parsed.explanation: Rating reflects a combined regime where protective state law substantially reduces everyday lodging, services, document and care friction, but national border screening, document-marker rules, facility restrictions and custody practice remain traveller-facing and severe. For an adult alone, entry can be outed, refused or subjected to lifetime-fraud analysis; local state protections help after arrival. For a trans minor with guardian, state shield care is meaningful, yet federal school, document, hospital-record and detention pressures create residual major exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules make mismatched sex markers on visas/passports an entry risk: additional evidence, refusal, possible lifetime-fraud analysis. Airport secondary screening may out travellers. Existing X passports remain valid but scrutinised.
entry_documents.protection: State X licences/IDs/birth certificates; anti-discrimination law reduces local ID friction; court challenges and legal-aid FAQ on passport/document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: State acceptance does not alter federal border screening or visa adjudication; visitor still passes national entry controls.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National custody documents conversion-therapy-style conditions, denial of care, forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse in immigration custody; reporting of trans prisoners stopped. Other-state arrest included men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State anti-discrimination and hate-crime law; panic defences abolished.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Local protections do not offset federal, immigration or correctional custody if visitor is detained.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars identity-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; some states criminalise bathroom use, with first arrest. Conflict with state protections at federal or national sites is unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State Most Protective tier: public accommodation, education and services protected; no mapped state facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private and state venues may be safer; federal/national facilities or funding conditions can still impose birth-sex restrictions.

care_services.exposure: National orders pressure youth care, block funding and subpoena hospital records for patients under 19; reimbursement threats; care-seeking families may face scrutiny.
care_services.protection: State covers gender-affirming care and has shield law protecting patients/providers from state charges or investigation for care legal here.
care_services.interaction: Shield helps locally; unclear whether it limits federal records demands, funding rules or visa screening.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism language prioritises radical pro-transgender groups; DOJ memo links radical gender ideology to violence; military/school orders hostile; public opinion supports birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime enhancements, anti-discrimination law, judicial review, civil-rights challenges.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing can raise border/police suspicion; local equality law constrains ordinary service denial.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face facility and school scrutiny; guardians' documents can trigger checks; national care/school orders and hospital subpoenas create privacy risk.
minors_guardians.protection: Shield law supports families seeking care legal in state; public-accommodation, education and X-document protections.
minors_guardians.interaction: State may be care destination; federal entry and records exposure remain, especially for foreign minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific traveller street-violence or police-stop data; national hostility and polarised opinion may enable harassment; custody abuse documented if interaction escalates.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalties, panic defences abolished, anti-discrimination law; no documented local service denial.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street friction could trigger police; if detention follows, federal/custody harms dominate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Visa refusal/fraud hard to challenge quickly; facility/custody remedy not shown to stop harm; shield scope unresolved; enforcement data missing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing court challenges, ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ, state anti-discrimination and hate-crime recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow/partial and do not cancel combined federal/local operative regime.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A is lower because its border order categorically excludes visibly trans visitors with no effective remedy. This regime is similar at documents but adds protective state lodging, care and X markers, and fraud is not automatic; higher safety.

0.55-B has comparable border secondary screening and refusal, but only administrative humiliation and return transport. Here lifetime-fraud risk plus national custody abuse raise severity; protective state law lowers local friction; net slightly lower.

0.75-C allows matching-passport entry and civil tribunal oversight. Here national document/entry hostility is active, though the state's protective tier and shield law resemble it locally; overall materially lower due to federal port and custody exposures.

parsed.synthesis: Combined operative regime is bifurcated: once inside the protective state, public accommodation, X documents, hate-crime law, and care-shield reduce routine risk, especially for families seeking care. But national ports, passports/visas, government-funded facility rules, correctional/immigration custody and counterterrorism framing are not cancelled by state law. Therefore safety is conditional: strong local mitigations are meaningful, while discovery at entry or in custody can produce stranding, permanent ineligibility, humiliation, care denial or abuse.
